full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** The clumping is documented behaviour of an essentially identical published model. The "type segregation" score is almost certainly an artifact, because the rule never uses type. I agree with the first pass on the mechanism. I upgrade its "variant of a known model" to KNOWN because a nearly exact published equivalent exists.

**1. The rule is the Local Attraction Model (Strömbom 2011).** Each agent turns toward the centre of mass of neighbours within a fixed radius, at constant speed, with noise, and nothing else. That is the core of Strömbom's model, and he described attraction as the only social force between individuals. The paper reports that it generates three different phases: swarms, undirected mills and moving aligned groups. Later work calls it the simplest model known to produce all three of these groups. A follow-up found that polarized group formation can be switched off in the LAM by implementing a fully synchronous version of the model. In this case only no group, mills and swarms are produced. Your description sounds synchronous, all agents updating each step. That fits the "swarm / no group" side, so plain clumping (nearest-neighbour ratio 0.3) is the expected outcome. The model is still studied as a family, e.g. Strömbom et al., "The shape and dynamics of local attraction", EPJ ST 2015.

Small differences that don't change the behaviour category:
- Strömbom's model includes an inertia term and a particular update order. Your version seems to have neither.
- The density is fixed at 1 agent per unit area on a wrap-around box, rather than a free group.

**2. The type segregation is very likely an artifact.** Types are assigned at random and never enter the rule. So the dynamics are exactly symmetric under swapping labels, and the expected type mix in any cluster equals the global mix. Nothing in the rule can sort agents by type. A score of 6.0 most likely comes from:
- **Small-cluster sampling noise:** tight clumps of a few agents will often be by chance mostly one type. A metric that isn't compared against a label-shuffled baseline on the same positions reads that as segregation.
- **Inherited starting patterns:** with sharp attraction and low noise, clumps can freeze around their initial random composition. That is persistence of chance, not sorting.

**3. Genuine or trivial?** The aggregation is real and well documented. The type sorting is not a real effect. Two checks would settle it:
- Shuffle the labels on the final positions and recompute the score. I expect the observed 6.0 to fall inside the shuffled distribution.
- Confirm the score doesn't grow over time beyond what shrinking cluster size alone would produce.
